paper_title: Astrophysical limits on very light axion-like particles from Chandra grating spectroscopy of NGC 1275
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: Paper presents new measured exclusion limits on axion-like particle (ALP) photon coupling from Chandra grating spectroscopy of NGC 1275 in the Perseus cluster. The 99.7% credible region limit is gaγ < 6.3 × 10^-13 GeV^-1 (Model-A) and gaγ < 7.9 × 10^-13 GeV^-1 (Model-B) for masses m_a < 1 × 10^-12 eV. This is a mass-independent (flat) bound valid over the range m_a < 1 × 10^-12 eV, encoded as a horizontal line. The paper notes this is the most stringent limit to date on g_agamma for very light ALPs. Model-A limit (6.3e-13) is used as the primary constraint. The limit applies to all masses below 10^-12 eV; the paper states 'for masses m_a < 1 × 10^-12 eV' and earlier 'with mass < 10^-11 eV'. The bound is mass-independent in the sense that the coupling limit does not vary significantly with mass in the probed range. At 95% confidence level for Model-B, the analysis picks out a preferred non-zero value of gaγ ≈ 4−8 × 10^-13 GeV^-1, but the authors attribute this to residual calibration errors rather than a detection.
